newsitem.title: INDIA: India communists, opposition oppose oil price rise.
newsitem.headline: India communists, opposition oppose oil price rise.

text.p: The Communist Party of India (CPI), part of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's governing coalition, said on Monday that a rise in petroleum prices and sugar would be an "ill-advised step".
The right-wing Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) also came out against a rise in petroleum product prices.

"It is an ill-advised step at this juncture when the rate of inflation has crossed 7.5 percent and the prices of wheat and atta (wheat flour) are already high, causing misery to the common people," the Press Trust of India quoted a CPI statement as saying.
The CPI said it "is therefore of the view that (the) government should not go for any hike in the price of sugar and petroleum products, rather it should seek other options".
Newspapers have speculated that the government may raise the prices of petroleum products and sugar.
United News of India quoted BJP spokeswoman Sushma Swaraj as saying the opposition party would launch protests if petroleum prices were increased.

India's year-on-year inflation rate measured by the wholesale price index rose to 7.65 percent in the week ending December 28 from 7.58 percent in the previous week, the Industry Ministry said on Sunday.
